                             REBUTTAL TESTIMONY OF KELLY WELLS

 1                                       I.   INTRODUCTION

 2   Q.     PLEASE STATE YOUR NAME, BUSINESS ADDRESS, AND OCCUPATION.

 3   A.      My name is Kelly Wells. My business address is: Lower Colorado River Authority

 4          (LCRA), 3505 Montopolis Drive, Austin, Texas 78744. I am employed by LCRA as a

 5          Regulatory Case Manager, Lead and am providing testimony in this docket on behalf of

 6          LCRA Transmission Services Corporation (LCRA TSC).


 7   Q.     ARE YOU THE SAME KELLY WELLS THAT PROVIDED DIRECT TESTIMONY

 8          IN THIS DOCKET?

 9   A.     Yes. I previously submitted direct testimony in this proceeding on behalf of LCRA TSC

10          in support of the Joint Application of LCRA TSC and Oncor Electric Delivery Company

11          LLC (Oncor) to amend their Certificates of Convenience and Necessity (CCN) for the Bell

12          County to Big Hill 765-kV Transmission Line Project (the “Project”).


13   Q.     WAS YOUR REBUTTAL TESTIMONY PREPARED BY YOU OR BY

14          KNOWLEDGEABLE PERSONS UPON WHOSE EXPERTISE, JUDGMENT, AND

15          OPINIONS YOU RELY IN PERFORMING YOUR DUTIES?

16   A.     Yes, it was.


17   Q.     IS THE INFORMATION CONTAINED IN YOUR REBUTTAL TESTIMONY

18          TRUE AND CORRECT TO THE BEST OF YOUR KNOWLEDGE AND BELIEF?

19   A.     Yes, it is.




     Rebuttal Testimony of Kelly Wells                                                      Page 3
  1   Q.         WHAT IS THE PURPOSE OF YOUR TESTIMONY?

 2   A.         The purpose of my rebuttal testimony is to respond to certain claims and contentions raised

 3              by several intervenor witnesses regarding the public involvement process and the notice

 4              provided by the Applicants in connection with this Project. My rebuttal testimony

 5              confirms that the Applicants complied with all applicable notice requirements under 16

 6              Texas Administrative Code (TAC) § 22.52 and, in fact, went beyond the minimum

 7              requirements of that rule in providing notice.


 8        II.       COMPLIANCE WITH 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4) AND EFFORTS EXCEEDING
 9                               THOSE REQUIREMENTS

10   Q.         PLEASE DESCRIBE THE NOTICE REQUIREMENTS.

11   A.         16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4) requires that a utility hold at least one public meeting prior to the

12              filing of its CCN application if 25 or more persons would be entitled to receive direct mail

13              notice of the application. Direct mail notice of the public meeting must be sent by first-

14              class mail to each person listed on the current county tax rolls as an owner of land within

15              500 feet of the centerline of a transmission line greater than 230 kilovolts (kV). Written

16              notice of the public meeting must also be provided to the Department of Defense Military

17              Aviation and Installation Assurance Siting Clearinghouse (formerly known as the

18              Department of Defense Siting Clearinghouse).


19   Q.         DID THE APPLICANTS COMPLY WITH THESE REQUIREMENTS?

20   A.         Yes, the Applicants fully complied with all applicable notice requirements under 16 TAC

21              § 22.52(a)(4). In fact, the Applicants exceeded those requirements in several significant

22              respects.




     Rebuttal Testimony of Kelly Wells                                                               Page 4
  1   Q.     PLEASE DESCRIBE HOW THE APPLICANTS EXCEEDED THE MINIMUM

 2          NOTICE REQUIREMENTS.

 3   A.      The Applicants exceeded the minimum requirements of 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4) in the

 4          following ways:

 5                  First, although 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4) requires only one public meeting, the

 6          Applicants held three public open house meetings for the Project. These meetings were

 7          held on June 16, 2025 at the Salado ISD Building in Salado, Texas; June 17, 2025, at the

 8          Lampasas ISD Old Middle School Cafeteria in Lampasas, Texas; and June 18, 2025, at the

 9          Menard County Community Center in Menard, Texas. Holding three meetings in different

10          communities along the project corridor provided potentially affected landowners multiple

11          opportunities to attend a meeting in their general area.

12                  Second, although 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4) requires notice to owners of land within

13          500 feet of the centerline, the Applicants expanded the notice area to include owners of

14          land crossed or within 520 feet of the centerline of the preliminary alternative route

15          links. This over-inclusive approach was adopted due to mitigate potential horizontal

16          accuracy limitations relating to county appraisal district data and aerial photography

17          interpretation when developing the preliminary route segments. On behalf of Applicants,

18          Oncor mailed the written notices of the public participation meetings by first-class mail.

19                  Third, in addition to the direct mail notice required by the rule, the Applicants

20          published notice of the public participation meetings in 11 newspapers of general

21          circulation in the counties within the project study area. Notices were published in the

22          Temple Daily Telegram, Burnet Bulletin, Eden Echo, Lampasas Dispatch Record, Mason

23          County News, the Brady-Standard Herald, Menard News and Messenger, San Saba News


     Rebuttal Testimony of Kelly Wells                                                           Page 5
  1          & Star, Eldorado Success, San Angelo Standard-Times, and Georgetown-Williamson

 2          County Sun on or about June 10–12, 2025. Publication in newspapers is not required by

 3          16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4) for public meeting notice, and this additional step further broadened

 4          the reach of the notice.

 5                  Fourth, the Applicants provided notice of the public meetings to the Department of

 6          Defense Military Aviation and Installation Assurance Siting Clearinghouse, as required by

 7          the rule, but also provided courtesy notice to identified pipeline companies within the

 8          project area and to certain federal, state, and local officials and agencies—none of which

 9          is required by 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4).

10                  Fifth, concurrent with holding the public meetings, both Oncor and LCRA TSC

11          activated public-facing project websites to describe the Project and the CCN process. The

12          Applicants also set up dedicated project email addresses and phone numbers to continue

13          gathering input and answering questions about the Project following the public

14          meetings. Upon request, Applicants’ representatives agreed to meet with individual

15          landowners or their representatives to better understand their specific concerns and

16          continue gathering input for evaluation of potential adjustments to the preliminary

17          alternative route links.


18                 III.    REBUTTAL TO CERTAIN INTERVENOR TESTIMONY

19   Q.     CERTAIN DIRECTLY AFFECTED INTERVENORS, SUCH AS RISSA PERSON,

20          ASSERT THAT THEY DID NOT RECEIVE NOTICE OF THE JUNE 2025 PUBLIC

21          PARTICIPATION MEETINGS. PLEASE RESPOND.

22   A.     In her testimony, Ms. Person asserts that she did not receive notice of the June 2025 public

23          participation meetings despite being affected by preliminary links G13 and F24. While I

     Rebuttal Testimony of Kelly Wells                                                           Page 6
  1          cannot confirm Ms. Person’s receipt of the notice, I can confirm that Ms. Person was

 2          included on the notice list for the mail-out that was sent on June 5, 2025, in advance of the

 3          June 2025 public participation meetings. Notice was sent to Ms. Person by first-class mail,

 4          consistent with the requirements of 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4).

 5                  Additionally, as I described in Section II above, notice of the public participation

 6          meetings was published in 11 newspapers of general circulation within the project study

 7          area on June 10–12, 2025. These published notices provided an independent and

 8          supplemental means by which any potentially affected party could learn about the

 9          upcoming meetings.

10   Q.     MULTIPLE INTERVENORS, SUCH AS JOHN BURROW AND BRENT

11          CABANISS, TESTIFY THAT THEY DID NOT RECEIVE A NOTIFICATION

12          PACKET IN ADVANCE OF THE JUNE 2025 PUBLIC PARTICIPATION

13          MEETINGS. PLEASE RESPOND.

14   A.     In accordance with 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(4), the Applicants’ direct mail notice of the public

15          participation meetings was sent to owners of property crossed or within 500 feet of the

16          centerline of the preliminary alternative route links. Landowners that were outside of these

17          parameters would not have been included on the mailing list for the public meetings.


18   Q.     MR. BURROW AND MR. CABANISS ALSO TESTIFY THAT THEY DID NOT

19          RECEIVE NOTICE OF THE PROJECT UNTIL APRIL 2026. PLEASE RESPOND.

20   A.     As described in Section 6.0 of the Environmental Assessment and Alternative Route

21          Analysis (EA), several route links were added or modified following the public

22          participation meetings based on public input, updated data, and further field investigation,

23          which resulted in new landowners becoming directly affected. All such landowners were


     Rebuttal Testimony of Kelly Wells                                                            Page 7
 1           provided with notice in accordance with 16 TAC § 22.52(a)(3). For additional discussion

2           on notice or supplemental notice of the Application, refer to Ms. Casey Petty’s rebuttal

3           testimony.

4    Q.     REBECCA FRENCH TESTIFIES THAT THE NOTICE DID NOT INDICATE

 5          URGENCY. PLEASE RESPOND.

 6   A.     The notice rules in 16 TAC § 22.52 require that direct mail notice of the public participation

 7          meetings and of the Application filing be sent by first-class mail. There is no requirement

 8          under this notice rule that notices denote the matter is “urgent” or bear any particular

 9          marking on the exterior of the envelope beyond what is necessary for proper delivery via

10          first-class mail. The Applicants complied with the rule by sending notice by first-class

11          mail to each person identified as an owner of directly affected land on the current county

12          “tax rolls.”

13                  Furthermore, the effectiveness of the notice process is demonstrated by the record

14          in this proceeding. Ms. French filed her motion to intervene in this docket on April 15,

15          2026, well ahead of the April 27th intervention deadline, and filed testimony.


16                                        IV.     CONCLUSION

17   Q.     PLEASE SUMMARIZE YOUR REBUTTAL TESTIMONY.

18   A.      The Applicants fully complied with all applicable notice requirements under 16 TAC

19          § 22.52. In fact, the Applicants exceeded those minimum requirements. While the notice

20          rule requires only one public participation meeting, the Applicants held three. While the

21          rule requires notice to landowners within 500 feet of the centerline, the Applicants

22          expanded the notice area to 520 feet. To facilitate public engagement, the Applicants

23          published notice in 11 newspapers of general circulation of the public participation


     Rebuttal Testimony of Kelly Wells                                                             Page 8
 1          meetings, provided courtesy notices to pipeline companies and government officials,

2          maintained public-facing project websites, and established dedicated email addresses and

3          phone numbers. As discussed above, the routes in the Application differ from those at the

4          public meetings because the Applicants did exactly what the public involvement process is

5          designed to do—gather public input and refine the routes accordingly. Finally, the fact that

6          all of the witnesses whose testimony I have addressed intervened and filed testimony in

7          this proceeding confirms that the Applicants’ notice process achieved its objective.


8   Q.     DOES THIS CONCLUDE YOUR REBUTTAL TESTIMONY?

9   A.     Yes, it does.




    Rebuttal Testimony of Kelly Wells                                                             Page 9
